rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: **Electric current.** Current is the rate of flow of charge, I = q/t; its SI unit is the ampere (1 A = 1 C/s) and conventional current is taken from positive to negative.  ·  **Drift velocity.** Free electrons gain a tiny average velocity v_d along the field between collisions: v_d = eEτ/m = eVτ/(ml); it is of the order of mm/s even in strong currents.  ·  **Relation I = nAev_d.** In time t electrons move v_d·t, so the charge crossing area A is q = nAev_d·t, giving I = nAev_d, where n is the number of free electrons per unit volume.
